cards.title: Probably not broken
cards.body:
When a device crawls or says it's full, it can feel broken. Usually it isn't.

Most slow or full devices need a **few minutes of tidying**, not a repair shop. And now that you know what RAM, storage and the CPU do, you can work out which one is struggling.

cards.title: The fix-it loop
cards.body:
Technicians fix problems with a simple loop:

1. **Describe** exactly what's wrong. "Slow" is vague. "Slow when 30 tabs are open" is a clue.
2. **Guess** the most likely cause.
3. **Try** the simplest, safest fix first.
4. **Check** whether it worked. If not, go back to step 2.

Common causes of a slow device: too many apps or tabs open (full RAM), too many **startup apps** (apps that open by themselves when it switches on), and heat.

One rule before any fix: **never delete something unless you're sure it's backed up or not needed.**

cards.prompt: Your laptop has been getting slower all afternoon.

choices.text: Open the task manager to see what's busy

choices.consequence: Booster apps rarely help, and some are junk or worse. Find the cause first.
That's a very expensive guess. The fix is probably free.

steps.text: The task manager shows **RAM 97% full**. You have **30 browser tabs** open. What's the simplest fix?

choices.text: Close the tabs you don't need
choices.consequence: Each tab uses RAM. With fewer open, the laptop speeds up. Check: it's working!
Photos are in storage. The problem was RAM, so nothing changes.

cards.explanation: Describe, guess, try, check. The task manager showed **full RAM**, so the fix was closing tabs. Deleting files only frees **storage**.

cards.title: What's safe to delete
cards.body:
When storage is full, go for big things you don't need:

- files that are **backed up** somewhere else (like the cloud)
- **duplicates**, like five blurry copies of one photo
- apps you **never use** (you can reinstall them later)
- **setup files** for apps you've already installed

Keep anything that's your **only copy**, anything you still need, and any **system file** you don't recognise: deleting those can stop the device working.

cards.prompt: This phone is completely full. Free up at least **15 GB**, but **keep your photos and your homework**.
cards.explanation: Big things you don't need are the quickest wins. The game plus the old downloads free 15 GB, and so do the backed-up videos on their own. Photos and homework were never in danger.

cards.prompt: Tidying up storage. Is each one **safe to delete** or one to **keep**?

items.label: Setup files for apps already installed
An app you haven't opened in a year
Blurry copies of the same photo
Your only copy of family photos

cards.explanation: Delete things that are **backed up, duplicated or unused**. Keep anything that's your **only copy**, anything you still need, and any **system file** you don't recognise: deleting those can stop the device working.

cards.prompt: Put the fix-it loop in order.
cards.explanation: **Describe, guess, try, check.** If the check fails, you loop back and try the next most likely cause.

cards.prompt: Your laptop takes five minutes to start, then crawls for a while after.

steps.text: The task manager has a **Startup** list with **15 apps** that open by themselves when the laptop switches on. What's the likely cause?

choices.text: Too many apps starting at once
choices.consequence: Yes. They all fight for the CPU and RAM just as you're trying to start.
Brightness affects the battery, not how fast the laptop starts.

choices.text: Stop the apps you don't need from starting
choices.consequence: They still work when you open them. They just don't all start at once.
That's the one to keep. It protects you from the moment you log in.

choices.text: Delete the system files that load first
choices.consequence: Then the laptop might not start at all.

cards.explanation: **Startup apps** open by themselves when the device switches on. Turning off the ones you don't need makes starting up faster. Keep security software running, and never delete system files.

cards.prompt: An update needs **12 GB free**. Make room without losing anything that **isn't saved somewhere else**.
cards.explanation: Music is in the cloud, the videos are backed up, and maps can be downloaded again, so deleting those three frees enough. The photos and notes are your **only copies**, so they stay.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- Use the loop: **describe, guess, try, check**.
- **Slow?** Check the task manager. Full RAM means closing apps or tabs; too many **startup apps** means a slow start.
- **Full?** Delete big things that are backed up, duplicated or unused. Keep your only copies and system files.

Next: batteries, chargers and heat.
